headline: On a full shop page the css-prop fold (`next-yak-css-9.7`) leads SSR, payload and scaling at or below hand-written `vanilla`, while the runtime hashers pay per tile: `emotion` renders the page 7.4× slower and injects a sheet that forces reflow on every client phase.

microbench.why: The css-prop fold emits one flat className per element and no styling runtime, so `next-yak-css-9.7` renders the 400-tile page at 0.322 ms/1k, under `vanilla` (0.327). The styled API's perf runtime holds its library slice to 0.285 ms and lands at 0.401 ms/1k, and `StyleX` ships static atomic classes at 0.357. The runtime hashers pay per tile: `emotion`'s `murmur2` drives it to 2.37 ms/1k (7.4× the fold), `goober` 1.20 and `styled-components` 1.12, each re-deriving a class for every tile's rule set.

autocannon.why: Under sustained load the single-class fold serves 281 req/s, within 1% of `vanilla` (280), because each request writes flat markup and touches no sheet. The styled perf runtime holds 253 req/s; the runtime libraries fall away as their per-request serialize repeats, `styled-components` 121 req/s, `panda` 107, `emotion` 73.0.

attribution.why: `vanilla` renders the page in 1.94 ms with no library slice; the css-prop fold matches at 2.04 ms (library 0.159 ms) because it ships the same flat classes. The styled perf runtime adds a residual `Yak` per styled tile (library 0.285 ms, 2.38 ms total). The hashers dominate their own render: `emotion` spends 7.76 ms of 14.4 ms in the library, `styled-components` 3.56 ms in `generateAndInjectStyles`, `goober` 3.43 ms recompiling and rehashing per tile.

hydrate.why: Extracted and atomic lanes hydrate as pure JS with no style, layout or paint, so `panda`, the css-prop fold and `vanilla` cluster at 56.6-58.5 ms; the styled perf runtime's slightly heavier tree brings it to 62.6 ms. The runtime hashers inject their sheet during hydration and force reflow, `emotion` 132 ms, `styled-components` 247 ms, `goober` 255 ms, roughly 4× the extracted floor.

inp.why: A wishlist toggle re-renders one tile subtree; the flat-class lanes do it in 8.40-9.50 ms and the css-prop fold and `vanilla` tie fastest at 8.40 ms. The styled perf runtime's residual wrappers cost it 10.0 ms. The hashers re-touch their sheet on the interaction, `styled-components` 28.6 ms, `goober` 33.4 ms, `emotion` 49.6 ms.

mount.why: Cold mount parses one static sheet for every extracted and atomic lane, so `vanilla`, the css-prop fold and `panda` land at 131-133 ms with the styled perf runtime a hair behind at 135 ms. The runtime libraries pay first-inject on top, `styled-components` 208 ms, `goober` 215 ms, `emotion` 245 ms.

renderTiming.why: One style recalc for every lane; the styling method changes nothing on the paint path for a page rendered once. The Chrome styleMs spread (0.690-0.721 ms among the static lanes) tracks page size, not technique, and the runtime libraries' higher figures come from parsing their injected sheet, not extra recalcs.

payload.why: The css-prop fold ships one class per element and almost no runtime, 7.20 kB gzipped, under `vanilla` (7.88 kB); the styled perf runtime carries its wrapper runtime at 8.30 kB. Atomic and utility lanes are far heavier, `goober` 11.2 kB, `StyleX` 13.0 kB, `styled-components` 21.2 kB, `tailwind-merge` 26.6 kB, `cnfast` 27.6 kB shipping the Tailwind sheet.

nsweep.why: At 4000 tiles the css-prop fold reaches 18.4 ms, under `vanilla` (19.0 ms), holding the flat-class shape as the grid grows; the styled perf runtime's per-tile wrapper costs it 22.3 ms. The hashers compound with count, `goober` 69.0 ms, `styled-components` 71.1 ms, `emotion` 133 ms, 6× the fold.
